## ROLEPLAY RULE 6. Do not metagame; Obey the Metashield.
Metagaming is a term used to describe actions based on knowledge during a round that would be inaccessible to your character. You cannot use information gained while you were playing a different character, while you’re a ghost, dead, in critical condition, or reveal information about who caused your death.
### Knowledge about antagonists (Metashield)
Awareness of what antagonists are capable of doing does generally not count as metagaming. The metashield prevents you from being able to use some information as an unfair advantage, including searching a PDA for uplinks without legitimate reason to suspect that the PDA was tampered with, or identifying chameleon gear without roleplay reasons (such as finding chameleon fibers.) Preparing for threats with no roleplay justification does sometimes count as metagaming, (such as hiding items linked to objectives and making them near impossible to retrieve.) To outline more specific issues with some roles that ARE metashielded: The objectives of the antagonist role of Space Ninja, are metashielded. Your character cannot know their intentions on station without explicitly seeing them. This means that characters should not go out of their way to guard or protect objective items (such as the R&D server or communication consoles), unless your character explicitly sees the antagonist attempting to interract with an objective. Zombies, in their entirety, are NOT metashielded (this includes associated reagents such as romerol, ambuzol, and ambuzol+). However, characters should consider the likelihood that an outbreak will occur, unlikely at most. Nuclear operatives are known, but characters should consider the possibility of ever meeting the dreaded group, VERY SLIM. Characters can maintain memories of encounters, but following rounds return to the mentality of the possibility being extremely low.
### Knowledge about Central Command personel and Protocol related to contract termination
The existence of Code Epsilon is NOT known by characters outside of Central Command; Contract termination from failure to comply with Central Command orders potentially escalating to violence, is known. The existence of code "Phoenix Down" IS known, and that compliance with instructions is mandatory in the event it must be called. The CONTINUED existence of the Deathsquad is only allowed to be a myth within the context of non-CC characters. For all station-goers, Deathsquad is known as defunct due to the questionable-at-best legality. Simply put, requests should not mention the Deathsquad at all, including emergency calls. ERT is the only known supporting force for stationwide emergencies necessitating external assistance.
### Knowledge gained out-of-character (OOC)
No in-character (IC) information should be shared via LOOC/OOC, and no actions should be taken or altered because of LOOC or OOC chats, including deadchat.
### Knowledge from past lives
When playing as a different character (such as taking a ghost role), you are to act without knowledge of what occured in the round as any prior characters and as a ghost. Mindswap spells, and polymorphs are not considered changing characters for this rule. Brain implantation, cloning and borging applies knowledge lost upon death (NLR).
### Knowledge gained while in crit, knowledge lost upon death (New Life Rule, NLR)
Being unconscious (critically injured, asleep, or dead) prevents your character from remembering anything that happened to or around them while unconscious. If brought out of critical state to alive state, you may remember what caused you to enter critical state. Entering the dead state causes your character to forget the direct cause of their death. This includes who killed them, incriminating details such as any actions or events that immediately lead to their death.
### Knowledge that the round will end (and how your character will cease to exist)
Your character should or may be aware that their current shift will end and they they will return to Centcomm. They do not know that this represents the effective end of their existence from the perspective of their player. You cannot prepare for end-of-round griefing (EORG) or perform other actions that only make sense in the context that your character’s life ultimately doesn’t matter.
